articles.title: Exeter University-led £20m project to prevent and detect dementia
articles.summary: The BRAINIAC hub involves 10 UK brain health clinics to diagnose, prevent and treat dementia.
articles.body:
A multi-million pound research hub is set to build artificial intelligence (AI) and data systems in a bid to prevent and detect dementia.

The BRAINIAC Hub, led by the University of Exeter, is funded by £10m from the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), part of UK Research and Innovation. Another £10m will be contributed by industry, charity and NHS partners.

The university said the hub would develop AI combining brain imaging, genetics, blood biomarkers and digital cognitive tests into a "single, clear picture of a person's brain health".

The funding covers a six year project with the first clinics to start operating in 2029, initially open to people via NHS referral.

It said BRAINIAC - AI and Emerging Technologies for Next Generation Brain Health Clinics - brings together 11 universities and 10 NHS sites over six years.

It said it would involve 10 brain health clinics across the UK to create one of the biggest research platforms into what really works to diagnose, prevent and treat dementia.

The clinics aim to help reduce risk and halve the time of getting a dementia diagnosis.

BRAINIAC director David Llewellyn, professor of clinical epidemiology and digital health at the university's medical school, said detection was the "hardest problem".

"The tools we build in these NHS clinics will let us pick up the first signs before symptoms show, and offer people a personalised prevention plan to help them keep their brains sharp for longer," Llewellyn said.

According to the university, about 982,000 people in the UK live with dementia.

It said the number was set to reach 1.4m by 2040, with the annual cost set to more than double to £90bn.

It said UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) has committed up to £80m for researchers to develop tools which could support diagnosing 92% of people referred with suspected dementia within 18 weeks by 2029.

The hub aims to make assessment and diagnosis 30% to 50% faster and identify more than 40% of the people it assesses at early-risk - before symptoms develop.

Deputy director Chris Fox, professor of clinical psychiatry at the university medical school and a practising clinician, said current treatments only help if people were diagnosed early.

"BRAINIAC will give the NHS the tools to do that at scale, designed with patients and clinicians from the start so they work in a busy clinic and not just on paper," Fox said.

The project brings together several universities including Cambridge, Oxford, Newcastle, Swansea and Imperial College London. It also involves organisations such as Dementia UK and Alzheimer's Society.

BRAINIAC is one of five new hubs to be funded by across the UK.

Professor Charlotte Deane, executive chair of the engineering and physical sciences research council at UKRI, said the five hubs would "improve lives".

"They build on the proven success of our previous hubs, which are already translating cutting-edge research into real benefits, advancing healthcare innovation, including the world's first AI-assisted brain tumour surgery," she said.

"By working closely with patients, the NHS and industry, we're helping people live healthier lives and preventing ill health before it starts."

articles.body: SRINAGAR: With National Conference (NC) facing its biggest internal challenge in recent decades, party president Farooq Abdullah and Jammu & Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah held a meeting with 15 of the 25 rebel MLAs at the former’s residence for over two hours on Friday morning in a bid to defuse the crisis.While Farooq sought to mollify the rebels by terming their demands “genuine”, Omar sought to play the emotional card by offering to resign several times during the meeting, construing the criticism of his cabinet ministers and his adviser Nasir Aslam Wani as akin to questioning his leadership. He walked out of the meeting at least three times before being persuaded by the MLAs to return, sources said.While the rebels’ key demands — replacing all eight ministers, including deputy CM Surinder Choudhary, and removing Wani — remained unresolved, the meeting agreed on setting up consultative committees of legislators for each cabinet minister and a separate manifesto committee to monitor the implementation of the party’s election promises, including the restoration of J&K’s special status, sources said.This is the first time in around four decades that NC MLAs have openly challenged the party leadership, creating a crisis for the Omar govt.After the meeting, Farooq, flanked by Omar and the MLAs, addressed media persons and dismissed suggestions of a split or rebellion within NC. The party remained “united and strong”, he asserted.“We have spoken to the legislators, and their concerns and grievances are genuine. We will give due consideration to them. Everyone was heard patiently. Some (confidence-building) measures will be taken soon, while others will be implemented gradually. We will work to strengthen the party and the govt so that people’s problems are addressed,” he said.The NC chief reiterated that the party would continue its fight for the restoration of statehood and Article 370.Bashir Ahmad Shah Veeri, MLA from Bijbehara in south Kashmir, said, “We remain committed to Article 370. It took BJP almost 70 years to declare it done and dusted; our fight (for its restoration) has not even completed four years so far ... you will see in the coming days how aggressively we pursue the restoration of statehood.”Another rebel legislator told TOI that the party leadership had agreed to consider a cabinet reshuffle within a year. “The meeting went well and I think all our demands to strengthen the party were accepted,” he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Not a fan of body lotion? An in-shower moisturizer may be the alternative you need
articles.summary: In-shower moisturizers, balms and butters make keeping your skin hydrated easier than ever — I asked a dermatologist for the best ones to try.
articles.body: As someone who uses lotion daily and is extremely serious about avoiding ashy knees and elbows, I’m intrigued by in-shower body lotion. The concept is simple — it’s a moisturizer designed to be applied on wet skin at the end of a shower, rather than on dry skin after toweling off, says Dr. Michele Green, a board-certified cosmetic dermatologist in New York. While some of our editors swear by them, I was a bit more skeptical on how (and how well) they work. To get the scoop on all things in-shower moisturizing, I spoke to Green to find out more — below, a list of products to consider trying and what to keep in mind as you explore your options. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best in-shower body lotions and balms Below are the best in-shower body moisturizers, including recommendations from Green and favorites of NBC Selected staff. Best overall NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown tested Cyklar’s in-shower body balm, and says it quickly became a body care favorite of hers. “It really comes down to the application: It’s uncomplicated, and I simply rub it all over my damp skin and let it dry down,” she says. It also dries down quickly enough to layer with a lotion for extra moisture, however, Brown says it’s moisturizing enough to wear alone (helpful if you’re in a rush). The formula includes a moisturizing lipid complex, along with ceramides and coconut seed butter. Best for sensitive skin Green recommends Curel’s in-shower moisturizer if you want to reinforce your skin’s moisture barrier. The formula combines moisturizing ceramides with soothing vitamin E, and has a gentle formula that’s safe for sensitive skin, according to the brand. “Ceramides are lipids that naturally hold skin cells together and keep moisture in, so replenishing them on damp skin helps restore the barrier while locking in hydration,” she says. “Its lightweight texture absorbs quickly, making it a reliable everyday option for dry to normal skin.” Editor’s pick Brown has repurchased Hanni’s Splash Salve multiple times since testing it for a previous NBC Selected Wellness Awards. “I love using this after swimming laps when I’m tired and want to just get everything done in the shower,” she says. “And I’ve gotten many compliments on how soft my skin feels.” The salve is water-activated and transitions to a silky texture that spreads easily over the body, and includes hydrating glycerin, along with jojoba and coconut oils for healing dry skin, according to the brand. Best budget This lotion has a rich, creamy texture that Green says is ideal for those who prefer “a more indulgent feel.” The formula includes hydrating glycerin, along with cocoa butter to nourish the skin, according to the brand. “Cocoa butter is a dense, nourishing emollient that forms a protective layer on the skin, making this product particularly helpful for rough, dry areas such as the elbows, knees, and shins,” says Green. For best results, apply the lotion in the shower to wet skin after cleaning and rinse off. Best softening This body conditioner from Lush has moisturizing argan oil, along with Brazil nut oil to soften the skin, according to the brand. Shea butter also helps to seal the moisture into your skin, while damask rose soothes any irritation. It’s also loved by Lush customers — it has a 4.1-star average rating from over 370 reviews at Lush. To get the most out of the conditioner, while in the shower, spread the butter over your body after cleansing, rinse and pat dry, so the oils can absorb into your skin. Best with fragrance This moisturizer is made with shea butter oil to help soften and brighten skin, along with hyaluronic acid for plenty of hydration, according to the brand. It has a slight coconut fragrance, and reviewers, who gave the lotion a 4.7-star average from 4,950 ratings, call it the “easiest, most convenient way to moisturize every day.” Right after showering, apply the moisturizer to your skin while still wet, and pat dry for the best results. Best splurge Avene is one of our favorite French pharmacy brands, and this balm has a non-sticky formula that should be lightly massaged into the skin, according to the brand. It includes glycerin for hydration, along with shea and safflower seed oils, plus it absorbs quickly into the skin. The balm, which has a 4.7-star average from over 730 Amazon ratings, is also great for sensitive skin, with reviewers saying they experience all-day hydration with no irritation after using. How I picked the best in-shower body lotions and balms I made our list of in-shower body lotions with these factors in mind: Ingredients: The best in-shower lotions and balms contain one or more of three types of ingredients: emollients, humectants, and barrier-strengthening ingredients, says Green. Emollients, like shea butter, cocoa butter, squalane and other plant oils, help soften the skin and form a protective lipid layer that seals in moisture, she says. Humectants, like glycerin and hyaluronic acid, draw water into the outer layers of the skin, helping to boost hydration. Lastly, barrier-supporting ingredients like ceramides help repair and strengthen the moisture barrier and the skin’s natural protective layer, says Green.Texture: Since in-shower lotions need to be able to blend with water, they usually contain emulsifiers, which are ingredients that let water and oil mix, says Green. “When the balm is applied to wet skin, these emulsifiers cause the butters and oils to blend with the water on the skin’s surface,” she says. This transforms the balm into a lighter, usually milky texture that spreads and rinses off easily. However, a thin layer of oil/butter should still stay bonded to the skin after rinsing — which is why I made sure to include products with lightweight formulas that stay put post-shower without leaving a heavy or greasy residue. How to shop for an in-shower body lotion or balm Which skin issues can in-shower body lotions help? Dryness, mainly. Emollients help form a layer to keep moisture in the skin, since it’s already been hydrated during your shower, says Green. “This lipid layer acts as a seal, slowing transepidermal water loss, or the evaporation of moisture from the skin,” she says. Meanwhile, humectants like glycerin hold water in the outer layers of the skin — when combined with the emollient barrier, it can keep skin “feeling soft and moisturized for hours after showering,” she says. In-shower body balms can also address skin care concerns like dullness, texture and eczema by using targeted actives to tackle the issues. However, combining a balm with other body products like serums, toners and exfoliants can be most effective for targeting multiple issues at once. “For most people, the best results come from using these products together, applying a targeted serum or toner to areas of concern and relying on an in-shower balm or body cream to maintain overall hydration,” says Green. What are the best ingredients for an in-shower body lotion? The ingredients you look for in an in-shower body balm will depend on the issues you want to address. Usually, the formulas are already designed to address common dry skin concerns like dryness, flakiness, itchiness, post-shower tightness and more, along with helping to counter the skin-stripping effects of hot showers and cleansers, says Green. However, aside from general dryness, in-shower body balms can help with other skin concerns, including: If you’re struggling with irritation or flare-ups, Green suggests soothing additives like colloidal oatmeal and panthenol. Acne-prone or bumpy skin should reach for formulas with gentle, hydrating exfoliants like urea or lactic acid, which Green says can help smooth rougher skin patches and improve textural issues like keratosis pilaris.Sensitive or eczema-prone skin may need extra barrier support, which Green says ceramides and oatmeal-based formulas will help to reinforce. Meet our dermatology expert At NBC Selected, we work with experts who have specialized knowledge and authority based on relevant training and/or experience. We also take steps to ensure all expert advice and recommendations are made independently and without undisclosed financial conflicts of interest. Dr. Michele Green is a board-certified cosmetic dermatologist in New York City. Why trust NBC Selected? I am an associate SEO reporter for NBC Selected, covering skin care, wellness, sales and more. For this story, I spoke to a board-certified dermatologist about everything you need to know about in-shower moisturizers and balms, including recommendations on the best ones to try. articles.title: Israel closes Hebron’s Ibrahimi Mosque to Palestinians for Jewish holiday
articles.summary: Contested West Bank holy site is reopened exclusively for Israelis, deepening tensions over control of the mosque.
articles.body:
Israeli forces have closed the Ibrahimi Mosque in the occupied West Bank city of Hebron to Palestinian worshippers as thousands of Israeli settlers converge on the site for a Jewish religious celebration.

The Palestinian Ministry of Religious Endowments said worshippers and mosque employees had been barred from entering and the call to prayer suspended.

Mosque director Moataz Abu Sneineh told Al Jazeera that Israeli authorities intended to open the mosque’s prayer halls and courtyards exclusively to Israelis.

The closure, imposed on Friday afternoon and set to last until 10pm on Saturday, coincides with an annual Jewish observance to commemorate Sarah, a wife of Prophet Abraham, who is traditionally believed to be buried at the site.

Israeli troops tightened checkpoints and restricted movement across Hebron’s Old City, where the mosque is located, preventing some residents from entering or leaving their homes.

Israeli forces told The Jerusalem Post they expected about 20,000 visitors at the site for the Jewish holiday, with hundreds of security personnel deployed.

The Ibrahimi Mosque , known to Jews as the Cave of the Patriarchs, is revered by Muslims and Jews as the burial site of the Prophet Abraham and members of his family.

Under a 1997 Hebron Agreement signed between Israel and the Palestinian Authority, Israel assumed security control over the Old City, while Hebron’s Palestinian municipality holds planning and construction powers.

However, in June, Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announced a takeover of those powers, undermining Palestinian oversight of the holy site and raising fears that Israel was seeking to seize the site for exclusive Jewish use.

The closure comes just days after Israeli forces ended a 10-day siege of Hebron, which saw hundreds of arrests, 15 home demolitions and the displacement of more than 3,300 Palestinians.

Israeli settlers have steadily expanded their presence in Hebron’s Old City, seizing Palestinian properties and establishing new outposts under Israeli military protection.

articles.title: Father of young co-pilot killed in jet crash says recording shows she fought until the last minute
articles.summary: Allan Filgueiras spoke in a news conference Friday for the first time since the jet his daughter, Nathalia Filgueiras, was co-piloting crashed in Florida, killing everyone on board.
articles.body: Allan Filgueiras has listened to the distressing air traffic control call that recorded his daughter’s last words over and over again, searching for a clue as to what led the Learjet 60 jet she was co-piloting to crash in Florida on Sunday, killing all nine people on board. Instead, what he heard was how his daughter, 20-year-old Nathalia Filgueiras, valiantly fought until the very last minute to keep control of the aircraft, the father said. “She made me so proud,” Allan Filgueiras, who is also a pilot, said. “She showed me what it is to be a hero.” The father spoke for the first time since the tragic event at a news conference Friday alongside Stuart Grossman, an attorney representing the family. They focused on expressing their condolences to those close to the eight other people killed in the crash, emphasizing the importance of an investigation into what happened, and remembering Filgueiras’ daughter. “The purpose of this is to preserve not just her memory but her reputation,” Grossman said. “Nathalia was beyond an average pilot; she was extraordinary.” Inspired by her father, Nathalia Filgueiras was determined to learn how to fly planes. Allan Filgueiras was the one who began teaching his daughter first before she went on to earn her pilot’s license while still in high school. “When we were flying together, I used to instruct her. And then, she became my instructor,” Allan Filgueiras said of his daughter. “She was gifted, and my soulmate.” Grossman said she fell in love with flying because her father would take her up starting at the age of 12. “That compounds our tragedy, knowing this is where it all began,” the attorney said. Born into a Brazilian household in Boca Raton, Florida, Allan Filgueiras reminisced about teaching his daughter to speak Portuguese at home. When she was a 17-year-old senior at West Boca Raton Community High School, Nathalia Filgueiras got her private pilot’s license thanks to a program from the Palm Beach County School District, which paid for her to attend her school’s aviation academy. “She said, ‘Dad, can you believe that I would pay for this, but they’re actually paying me?’” Allan Filgueiras said, remembering how his daughter felt when she got into the program. “It was her happiest moment.” Grossman said he understands how many people might be surprised to learn that someone as young as 20 could be a co-pilot in a private jet. “But wait until you see her hours, and what the government proves about her capabilities,” the attorney said. “She was really special. This is a loss to aviation.” One of Nathalia Filgueiras’ flight instructors, Chris Kirk, told TODAY.com on Thursday that while the young pilot had remarkably good, innate skills to fly planes, she was known for showing up “overprepared” to complete her practical tests — which are required to receive specific pilot certificates. “She was at the top of her class in everything she did and she was perfectly qualified to be the co-pilot of this flight despite her tender years,” Grossman said. According to Grossman, the National Transportation Safety Board, which is investigating what caused the crash, sent 20 investigators to South Florida to look into what led to the tragedy. The pilot killed in the crash was identified as Capt. Jeff Gregory and had previously worked for East Coast Jets, the private jet charter company’s director, April Honnen, said on Facebook. The passengers killed were identified by relatives as Adam Robinson and Helen Sharp and their children, Emma, 4, and Charlie, 2. The other passengers were Rachael Reed, Charmi Fehr and Anita Maria Cetina, the families said on Facebook. NTSB investigators said on Thursday they have recovered parts of one of the Learjet 60 jet’s engines and are still excavating the crater left on the ground at the site of the crash in Greenacres. “We’re not making allegations against anybody at this time. We’re going to do the right thing. We’re going to listen to what the government uncovers. Then we’ll have our experts look at it and say they agree or not,” Grossman said. When Allan Filgueiras thinks back to the air traffic control call from Sunday, when his daughter warned that the jet was “descending 10,000 feet per minute” and about to crash, he wishes he could have been “by her side inside the plane to help, to be by her.” “It feels like someone is tearing the heart right out of my chest,” the father said. “I have to find a way to live and make it through.” “Nathalia doesn’t want to see a father falling apart,” he added. “I’m going to find a way to make her proud.”

articles.title: Pope Leo ‘proud to be an American’ and vote in US midterms
articles.summary: Pope Leo XIV has said he was proud to exercise his right to vote as an American in the recent US midterm elections.
articles.body: Pope Leo XIV has said he was proud to exercise his right to vote as an American in the recent US midterm elections. Speaking on board the papal plane to South America, the first US-born pope responded to a question from CNN about the significance of him voting. The pope’s decision to cast a mail-in ballot is likely the first time a pope has voted in secular, democratic elections. “I am proud to be an American, and exercise the right [to vote],” Leo XIV said. The pope did not give any reaction to the US midterm election results while on board and said “no comment” when asked about the outcome in Texas which saw the traditionally Republican state elect Democrat Senator James Talarico. Leo made his remarks as he both addressed and personally greeted journalists traveling with him from Rome to Montevideo on Friday. On October 30, the Vatican confirmed that Pope Leo had voted in the midterm elections, adding that he had always sought to vote when possible. The pope also referred to that statement when on board. Records show that, before his election as pontiff, Leo, whose baptismal name is Robert Prevost, has in the past voted in both Republican and Democrat primaries in Illinois. He also cast a vote in the 2024 election. While it is not known how Leo XIV voted, the Chicago-born pontiff has publicly disagreed with US President Donald Trump’s administration over issues such as the war in Iran and migration. The pope is embarking on the most significant visit of his papacy a little over 3 weeks since lung cancer surgery. Despite the intense schedule of the visit, the pope told reporters he had always been confident the trip would go ahead and praised his “wonderful” medical team. Leo XIV’s 12-day tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru is very intense and will see him covering 19,000 miles, give 36 speeches, participate in around 50 events. He will visit Cusco, which is more than 11,000 feet above sea-level and where there is 35% less oxygen per breath. “I know some people were doubtful about this trip taking place,” the pope told reporters. “I confess that from the first day I had no doubt, and was convinced, that this trip had to go forward.” He added that he was in “fairly good shape,” telling another reporter that he relies on “trust in God, good doctors and a healthy lifestyle.” According to the Vatican, doctors have said that Leo XIV’s cancer was detected at an early stage during routine checks, that the surgery successfully removed the cancer and that he needs no further treatment. The pope, speaking to a journalist from The New York Times, said that following his time in hospital he wanted to underline “how healthcare should be a right of all people.” He added that he felt “close to those who are sick.” Leo XIV, who likes to stay active and enjoys sports, said he planned to get back to playing tennis and told another reporter for Catholic outlet Our Sunday Visitor those who are facing a cancer diagnosis should not be afraid. He added that “early detection is obviously the best way to go” and that “regular checks are a blessing.” Addressing journalists collectively, the pope pointed out that the longest part of the visit was to Peru, the country he served as a missionary and bishop for around two decades. Leo added that he was “very happy to be going back there.” The pope also shared some jokes on board. A Reuters journalist asked the pope, given his recent meeting with Bob Dylan, if Leo could arrange for Bruce Springsteen to have a concert for Vatican journalists. “Some things are above my paygrade,” the pope joked.

articles.title: Hockey great Wayne Gretzky defends relationship with President Trump and speaks on Russian hockey ban
articles.summary: Wayne Gretzky spoke about his friendship with President Trump and Canada's decision to ban Russia from the World Junior Hockey Championship in Alberta.
articles.body: The Great One, Wayne Gretzky, is a unicorn in sports. He is not only the hockey GOAT (greatest of all time), holding dozens of records that many believe may never be broken. He is also beloved in both the United States and Canada. He's an Edmonton Oilers and Los Angeles Kings legend on the ice, but his relationship with President Trump and friendliness to the administration off the ice, has been considered a strain on that love and respect according to many Canadians in recent years. While at the grand opening of the Walter Gretzky Upper Deck Hockey Resource Center in Toronto, in honor of Wayne's father, Gretzky fielded questions about sports cards, collectibles, his father's legacy, his thoughts on how Canadians are not too fond of his friendly relationship with Trump, as well as how the Russia/Ukrainian War affects the sport of hockey. Gretzky discussed Upper Deck expanding its longstanding exclusive agreement with him, naming the "global icon" an Upper Deck Legacy Partner, joining NBA legend Michael Jordan. Jamie Dinsmore, President and CEO of the Hockey Hall of Fame said, "Wayne Gretzky’s impact on hockey extends far beyond records and championships, and we are honored to celebrate his enduring influence on our sport," Gretzky then fielded a few political questions. Speaking directly to his relationship with President Trump, "People can have their own opinions. That is what life is all about," Gretzky said. In the past, Gretzky has has defended his Canadian identity while insisting he prefers to stay out of politics, saying, "I'm just a hockey player," while trying not to be overly political. Gretzky has undoubtedly developed a close personal friendship with President Donald Trump over the decades. This is nothing new. Gretzky has frequently spent time with Trump at Mar-a-Lago in Florida. Gretzky is a Florida resident. Notably, his family attended Trump's 2024 election-night celebration and his January 2025 presidential inauguration, which didn't sit well with Canadians. Trump has also publicly praised "The Great One," even suggesting he run for Canadian prime minister. Their friendship has sparked backlash in Canada especially over the last few years, particularly over Trump's comments about making Canada the 51st U.S. state. That has led to Canadians booing the United States National Anthem and more animosity to between the two nations. Gretzky wrapped up his response by saying, "People are entitled to what they believe in and what their opinions are. It's as simple as that." PUTIN ACCUSES HOCKEY ORGANIZATIONS OF 'GROSS VIOLATION' AS CANADA BARS RUSSIA FROM WORLD JUNIORS A few minutes later Gretzky spoke about the ban of Russian and Belarusian teams from the upcoming World Junior Hockey Championship in Alberta as well as his candid thoughts on the war against Ukraine. "Nobody likes war, right?" Gretzky stated. "We definitely don't want to see this [war]. We hope it ends. We wish it didn't start." REPUBLICAN CONGRESSMAN PRESSES NHL OVER ALEX OVECHKIN’S APPEARANCE IN PUTIN PARTY CAMPAIGN AD The Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney made it clear recently that Russia and Belarus will not be welcome at the upcoming World Junior Hockey Championship in Alberta, declaring that as long as the war continues, "there will be none of those athletes competing for their countries in Canada." Meanwhile, six European nations, including Sweden, Finland and the Czech Republic, have threatened to boycott games against Russia, leaving international hockey facing a potential showdown between sports officials, national governments and the courts. In response to the questioning Friday and the Prime Minister's statements, Gretzky said, "I understand the stance the Prime Minister has taken and good for him." Gretzky also said, "I think a lot of the players and the people of Canada feel the same way." Gretzky, though he has ruffled feathers of Canadians for his clear friendly relationship with the commander in chief and the current administration, he is well-liked and respected and admired from the Canadians I've spoken with. He handled these questions with grace and transitioned smoothly back into stories about his father, buying the famous T206 Honus Wagner card, and his love for the games and for players like Connor McDavid. NEARLY $1M IN GRADED TRADING CARDS STOLEN FROM FEDEX TRUCK OUTSIDE PSA FACILITY IN SANTA ANA As for his father, moving on from the political talk at the behest of Upper Deck President Jason Masherah, Gretzky said, "My dad and my family mean everything to me, so the opportunity to honor him and showcase his impact to fans and collectors around the world is one that is close to my heart," said Wayne Gretzky. "I’m honored to be named an Upper Deck Legacy Partner by a company that has become like a second family to me over the decades we’ve worked together, and I’m looking forward to expanding this relationship for years to come." As stated in a press release from Upper Deck, the trading card and collectibles company "is marking the Legacy Partner distinction by introducing exclusive new collectibles, the "Upper Deck Master Collection – Wayne Gretzky" and a new Upper Deck Authenticated portfolio that will celebrate the story of Wayne Gretzky from the beginning of his career to the end, and all the accomplishments in between." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "For decades, we’ve worked to capture the moments that defined Wayne Gretzky’s unparalleled career. His impact on the game of hockey is impossible to measure by records alone, so we’ve worked to create collectibles that tell the story of the mark he left on hockey," said Masherah. "We’re honored to welcome Wayne as a Legacy Partner and celebrate the impact his family had on his life and career, as well as the impact Gretzky continues to have on hockey at all levels."

articles.title: Florida dad makes final FaceTime call to wife before dying in flash flood
articles.summary: Joshua Bennett's wife described a frantic FaceTime call from her husband as floodwaters trapped his truck on a Brevard County road before the line went dead.
articles.body: A Florida father died after his vehicle became trapped in flash floodwaters, with his wife now sharing the details of a desperate final call before his death. Joshua Bennett, 34, of Palm Bay, died Monday after heavy rainfall triggered flooding in Brevard County, along Florida's east-central coast. Bennett had reportedly left home to buy coffee when he encountered the rising floodwaters, according to WESH 2 News. MOM OF 2 WHO DIED RESCUING SONS DURING BAHAMAS SNORKELING TRIP IS IDENTIFIED His wife, Stacy Petit Bennett, told the outlet her husband called her in a panic as his truck became surrounded by floodwaters on San Filippo Drive. "He called me on FaceTime, and he was just crying, like, 'I don't know what to do, I don't know what to do,'" Stacy Petit Bennett said. "And he said he's in the middle of a river, and his car is, like, submerged with water all around." Stacy Petit Bennett urged her husband to break a window before the call abruptly disconnected. She said she called 911 and spent hours trying to get help for her husband. NURSE IMPALED BY POLE DURING HIKE FORCED TO TREK 10 MILES FOR HELP: 'A FREAK THING' Bennett's widow described him as an "amazing husband and dad." "Every life is important, and everyone deserves a chance to be rescued. To be saved. He was just 34 years old. His kids are young," she said, according to WESH 2 News. Bennett was a father of four, including three children with special needs, according to his wife. His children include twin daughters who were born prematurely. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER His wife said their children have been asking when their father would be coming home. "He's not here. I don't have my support system. They don't have their father," Stacy Petit Bennett said. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS Bennett was one of two people who died during the flooding in Brevard County. The other victim, Archie Richards, 78, was found dead inside his vehicle near Richards Lane and Hall Road, according to WESH 2 News, citing the Brevard County Sheriff's Office. articles.title: 'Israel, Middle East wouldn't exist today': Trump boasts of stopping Iran's nuclear ambitions
articles.summary: US president Donald Trump has claimed that Israel and the wider Middle East would not exist today had he not prevented Iran from acquiring a nuclear
articles.body: US president Donald Trump has claimed that Israel and the wider Middle East would not exist today had he not prevented Iran from acquiring a nuclear weapon, as Washington weighs the possibility of resuming military operations against Tehran. The development comes amid renewed diplomatic efforts to de-escalate tensions in the region.On Friday, in a post on his social media platform, Truth Social, Trump asserted that his intervention had prevented a threat to the region's survival."Israel and, in fact, the entire Middle East, WOULD NOT EXIST TODAY if I did not stop Iran from having a Nuclear Weapon. Nobody wants to say that, but everybody knows it’s true!" he wrote.The remarks come as Trump considers whether to authorise fresh military strikes against Iran. According to Fox News, the US President met his national security team on Wednesday and Thursday to discuss the possible resumption of military operations.Speaking to reporters in the Oval Office on Thursday, Trump said Washington would soon "make a decision" on the matter. Questioning whether further strikes were necessary to ensure Iran's nuclear programme was permanently dismantled, he said the objective was to ensure "it will never happen again"."I would rather not destroy the rest of the country if possible, but maybe I will have to. You'll know soon enough," Trump added.Separately, a US official told media outlets that the US Central Command (CENTCOM) was finalising preparations for a possible resumption of major military operations against Iran, although no formal orders had been issued by Washington.CENTCOM on Friday posted an image of an A-10 Thunderbolt II attack aircraft preparing for take-off at a military base in the Middle East. The command did not disclose the base's location or the aircraft's mission. The post came as Trump weighed further military action.Meanwhile, Trump spoke with Qatar's Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani by telephone on Friday to discuss efforts to ease regional tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler's media office.The two leaders discussed Qatar's mediation efforts towards reaching "a comprehensive agreement that ends the crisis and achieves security and stability in the region".Sheikh Tamim stressed "the importance of continuing dialogue and adopting diplomatic means to resolve disputes, sparing the region further escalation, and ensuring freedom of maritime navigation and the security of energy supplies", the statement said.Qatar has been mediating between Washington and Tehran, with Gulf Arab states seeking to prevent a renewed escalation after coming under Iranian fire during the conflict.In a separate diplomatic development, Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Faleh Al-Zaidi told Trump during a telephone conversation on Thursday that Iraqi territory must not be used to launch attacks against neighbouring countries."The Prime Minister affirmed Iraq's position calling for respect for the sovereignty of states, non-use of its territories as a launchpad for aggression against neighbouring countries," the Iraqi Prime Minister's Office said in a statement on X.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Louisiana woman alleged her uncle sold interests in nearly 300 acres from her mother's estate to himself; 23 years after her mother's death, an appeals court revived part of her lawsuit but vacated a $10,000 award
articles.summary: A Louisiana woman who accused her uncle of transferring interests in nearly 300 acres of land from her late mother's estate to himself has won another
articles.body: A Louisiana woman who accused her uncle of transferring interests in nearly 300 acres of land from her late mother's estate to himself has won another chance to pursue part of her lawsuit. The Louisiana Court of Appeal ruled on Wednesday that Jessica Gooden Walker could continue her claims concerning her uncle's handling of the estate. However, the court rejected her other claims and cancelled a $10,000 damages award she had previously received.As per the ruling, the dispute began after Walker's mother, Wilma Letitia Blake Gooden, died in 2003. Her will placed her estate into a trust for her two daughters, who were to share its benefits equally. Wilma appointed her brother, Robert E. Blake Jr., to manage both the estate and the trust.Walker later alleged that Blake had used his position to transfer interests in several properties in Rapides Parish, Louisiana, to himself. The properties involved nearly 300 acres of land. She claimed that he subsequently transferred or sold property interests to businesses connected to him without properly informing her.The legal battle began in 2013 when Walker sued her uncle over his handling of the estate and trust. More than a decade later, the appeals court has ruled that some of her allegations deserve further examination. It has not, however, decided whether Blake committed wrongdoing.How the property dispute beganAccording to court records, Blake carried out several property transactions in May 2005, while he was managing his sister's estate.One transaction involved exchanging shares in Emfield Development Corporation for estate property. The agreement valued six shares at $33,000 and the land at $6,450, with the estate making an additional payment of $26,550 to Blake.Another transaction transferred interests in two tracts of land from the estate to Blake for $104,534. Court documents show that a promissory note was involved rather than a direct cash payment.The estate's remaining assets were subsequently placed in the trust, and Blake was discharged from his responsibilities as executor in October 2005.The appeals court noted that Blake later sold properties and timber at a substantial profit in 2006 and 2007. It also found evidence of further transactions that financially benefited him.Walker maintained that she had not been properly informed about the sales. She said a letter received in July 2009 sought her approval of documents releasing Blake from claims against him, but did not clearly disclose the earlier property transfers.She refused to sign those documents. According to her court filings, she obtained more information in September 2012 and later searched public records, where she found documents relating to the transactions.Why the earlier court dismissed her claimsThe case continued for years as both sides disputed whether Walker had waited too long to bring her allegations before a court.Blake argued that the legal deadlines for filing claims had expired. A lower court eventually accepted that argument and dismissed most of Walker's claims.In June 2025, the lower court also awarded Walker $10,000 because Blake had failed to distribute trust assets on time. Walker appealed the dismissal of her claims, while Blake challenged the damages award.The main question before the appeals court was whether Blake's responsibilities as executor of the estate should be treated separately from his responsibilities as trustee. The distinction mattered because different legal deadlines applied to those roles.Appeals court allows part of lawsuit to continueThe appeals court agreed that Walker had filed her claims against Blake as trustee too late. It therefore upheld the dismissal of those claims.However, the judges found that the lower court had wrongly treated all the allegations as claims against Blake in his role as trustee.They explained that managing an estate and managing a trust were separate responsibilities, even when the same person performed both jobs.The court also found that the estate's final accounting had not received the required judicial approval. It said Blake could not waive that requirement himself when he was both executor and trustee, because of the conflict between those roles.As a result, the judges ruled that Walker's claims concerning his handling of the estate should not have been dismissed for being filed too late.They also rejected Blake's argument that Walker could not bring those claims because the trust, rather than Walker personally, had inherited the estate. As a beneficiary, she had an interest in how the estate was managed.The judges made clear that whether Blake acted improperly remains unresolved and must be examined in further proceedings.What happened to the $10,000 award?The appeals court separately considered the $10,000 Walker had received for delays in distributing trust assets. Under the trust arrangements, she was entitled to receive half her share on September 15, 2012, and the remainder on September 15, 2017.The judges agreed with the lower court that the assets had not been distributed on time. However, they found insufficient grounds in the record to support the specific $10,000 award.They therefore cancelled that amount and directed the lower court to reconsider the issue after a hearing and explain its decision.The appeals court also upheld the dismissal of Walker's claims under Louisiana's racketeering law.The case will now return to the lower court for further proceedings on her allegations concerning Blake's actions as executor.You use AI every day. articles.title: Meghan Markle’s father arrested in US over alleged child sex abuse photos
articles.summary: US authorities found sexually explicit photos that appeared to show Thomas Markle with prepubescent girls.
articles.body:
The estranged father of Britain’s Prince Harry’s wife, Meghan Markle, has been arrested in the United States on a charge of possession of child sexual abuse material.

The US Department of Justice on Friday announced that Thomas Markle Sr was arrested in Florida after law enforcement officers discovered “sexually explicit photographs” of him with prepubescent girls in two storage units, located in the Los Angeles area, that he rented for nearly two decades.

“Mr Markle allegedly targeted innocent children and sought to steal their innocence through his criminal actions”, Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) Director Kash Patel said on Thursday.

According to the Justice Department, authorities learned in October that an individual signed an affidavit stating they had discovered child sex abuse material among Markle’s possessions in the Philippines.

Law enforcement interviewed a separate individual who told them the 82-year-old had rented a storage unit near Los Angeles since 2008. Information gathered from the first individual led to the discovery of a second unit.

After receiving warrants, the Justice Department said FBI agents searched the two units registered to Thomas. Inside, they found 78 items, including photos, film negatives and books that contained explicit imagery of him with underage girls.

The affidavit described three of those photographs. Two showed a man, who a witness identified as Thomas, with a nude prepubescent girl. The third photo shows a nude underage girl in what appeared to be a Philippine hotel room.

Officials, according to the affidavit, also found photos that appeared to show Thomas with “children in various stages of undress”.

Thomas was living in the Philippines earlier this year when he suffered a stroke and had his left leg amputated. That forced him to return to the US.

Meghan issued a statement to The New York Times in October, saying she first learned of the allegations against her father in 2018, when a letter detailing them was sent to the unit of London’s Metropolitan Police that was handling her security then.

“I am deeply distressed at the news that has come to light in the last 24 hours,” the duchess of Sussex wrote to the Times in an apparent reference to reports by the Sun, a British tabloid, on the allegations. “My thoughts are with any children who may have been harmed.”

“I hope it can now be understood that, despite certain media publications’ distortion over the years, any distance from my father and my choice to not allow him to have contact with our children was for one reason: to protect them,” she added.

The arrest of Thomas comes as President Donald Trump’s administration has been criticised for its handling of cases related to the abuse of children, particularly the release of files on the investigation into convicted sex trafficker Jeffrey Epstein .

Last year, King Charles stripped Prince Andrew of his princely title as he tried to shield the royal family from the scandal surrounding his brother’s relationship with Epstein.

Meghan, Prince Harry and their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet, relocated back to the United Kingdom in August.

The Associated Press tried to reach Meghan’s representative on Friday but has not yet heard back.

Thomas Markle is expected to appear in a Florida court on Friday. If convicted, the Justice Department said he could face a maximum sentence of 20 years in a US federal prison.

articles.title: Protesters break into Microsoft data centre site in Amsterdam
articles.summary: Data centres face protests across Europe due to the massive amounts of computing power and water they use.
articles.body:
Protesters in the Netherlands have broken into a construction site for a new Microsoft data centre in Amsterdam, the latest action in a growing movement sweeping Europe.

Several hundred activists occupied the site in the Sloterdijk district on Friday, responding to a call for a two-day protest across Europe against data centres, which handle the large processing workloads associated with artificial intelligence (AI). Demonstrators clashed with police as some climbed a crane and set off flares.

Nathan Timmer, of the protest group Geef Tegengas – which translates as Push Back – told local broadcaster AT5 that demonstrators were occupying the site in an effort to stop construction.

“We don’t want it to be built. Nobody needs it,” Timmer said. “The only thing this will be used for is AI slop. AI warfare, data surveillance and committing genocide. We don’t want that.”

Pro-Palestinian activists also joined the demonstrations in the Dutch capital. By late afternoon police were escorting activists off the construction site, though some remained, local media reported.

Dutch police said they detained 150-200 people suspected of trespassing during the protest.

Microsoft said it was aware of the Amsterdam demonstration.

“We understand that people feel strongly about the project, and we respect their right to express those views peacefully,” a spokesperson said. “However, we do not condone any actions that are unlawful or that put people’s safety at risk.”

Data centres face resistance around the world due to the massive amounts of computing power and water they use. Activists argue that the boom in facilities serving cloud computing and AI is moving faster than public consultation and environmental oversight.

Dozens of civil society and grassroots groups have said they will join the “Stop Dirty Data Centres” events on Friday and Saturday in 15 European countries, including Ireland, Poland, Denmark, Finland, Spain, Italy, the Netherlands, France and the United Kingdom, organisers said.

In Germany, a dozen protesters gathered in front of a data centre on the outskirts of Berlin on Friday.

“We want to put a stop to this blind construction of data centres around Germany, regardless of any environmental concerns,” said protest spokeswoman Caro Weber. “This is really, really dangerous for our future.”

About 100 people also protested against data centres in front of the Polish parliament, representing communities around Warsaw where new centres are planned.

In Italy, the fast-growing data centre industry is facing an equally rapid rise in grassroots opposition, particularly in the northern Lombardy region, the country’s main hub for digital infrastructure.

articles.title: These are the 21 best collectible gifts of this year, according to shopping experts who are also collectors
articles.summary: I found the top collectible gifts for all ages and interests from Lego, Jellycat, Le Creuset and more.  Start or help grow your loved one’s collection this holiday season.
articles.body: When I’m figuring out what to get my loved ones as holiday gifts, I make a mental list of everything they collect. Candles, watches, vinyls, kitchenware, cameras — anything they can’t get enough of is sure to make them happy when they unwrap it. If my family members or friends haven’t started a collection yet, I help them do so, which is extra special. I love being the first person to buy them something, and watching their collection grow as they become more passionate about it is rewarding. Below, I rounded up a handful of collectible gifts you may want to surprise your favorite people with this year. I’ll continue updating my list over the next few weeks to offer additional suggestions. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best collectible gifts of 2026 This year, I’m giving Lego lovers in my life sets that include the rechargeable Smart Bricks and Smart Tags, which debuted earlier this year. The Smart Tags communicate with the Smart Bricks, telling them to react with lights, colors and sounds depending on how your giftee interacts with them. Pokémon’s Training House with Pikachu Lego set comes with one Smart Brick, four Smart Tags and a charger, giving your giftee everything they need to experience the innovation. They’ll use the included 400 pieces to put together all the figures, and learn how to use the Smart Play System from the directions and a companion app. Even if it feels like your recipient owns every type of candle, I can almost guarantee they haven’t seen anything like this set from Glasshouse Fragrances. It comes with the brand’s 13.4-ounce Kyoto in Bloom candle and a Spinning Carousel accessory, whose base sits on top of the jar so the festive charms hang above it. When your giftee lights the candle, the bright, flickering flame makes the dangling charms shimmer and twirl. They’ll also see the flame through the laser-cut windows on the sides of the festively decorated jar. I collect custom jewelry, and Catbird’s Confetti Charm Bracelet is one of my favorite pieces. Its dainty, minimalistic design is ideal for everyday wear, and I love that I have a connection to every detail. To personalize it for your giftee, you pick out the one, three, five or seven charms you think they’d find most meaningful on Catbird’s website. Then, jewelers in the brand’s Brooklyn studio add them to an adjustable chain and ship out the final handmade piece. You can choose from charms like letters, birthstones, zodiac signs and other symbols — each is priced individually. Lennox recently released a second edition of its highly coveted Spice Village after retiring the original one in the early ‘90s — if your loved one has always dreamed of owning it, help them get started with this set of six jars. In future years, you can buy them additional sets to build up to the complete collection of 24 jars, and even expand into the brand’s other matching pieces. Each spice jar is shaped like a Victorian house, hand-painted with pastel colors and labeled with a spice’s name. The Garden District Spice Village Set comes with jars for rosemary, oregano, basil, allspice, cinnamon and nutmeg. You can’t help but smile when you see a Jellycat, which is why it’s so easy to start collecting them. My favorite ones to give and receive are Amuseables, which are mini stuffies of animated objects like food and plants — there are even sports and weather themed ones. The Boiled Egg was my first Jellycat Amusable, and I’ve since gotten other iterations of it like a limited-edition Easter Bunny egg and a scientist. The stuffed toys are small, which makes them great desk or shelf decor, and they’re usually compact enough to fit inside a stocking. While Kodak’s Charmera isn’t as fancy or rare as the vintage cameras many collectors have their eye on, it makes for a fun gift that aligns with something they’re passionate about. It also takes quality photos — our team was impressed when we tested it. The tiny, rechargeable digital camera comes on a keychain, takes photos and videos, and lets your giftee download content directly to their phone using the included USB-C cable. (They can also plug the camera or its SD card into a computer — the SD doesn’t come with the camera, so consider buying one for them.) The Charmera lets your giftee choose from four frames and seven filters in photo mode, and they’ll be surprised by what their camera looks like when they open the package since it’s a blind box. My grandma has collected salt and pepper shakers for decades, which inspired me to do the same when I moved into my first apartment. My loved ones know that I’m always on the hunt for a quirky set, so they buy them for me during the holidays — perhaps you know someone who’d like them, too. Ban.do’s orange and orange juice carton shakers are exactly what I’d go for. Your giftee can display them on a shelf or make them part of their table’s centerpiece. And since they’re meant for dispensing seasonings, they’re functional in addition to being adorable. While some people are Funko POP! collectors, others have one of the brand’s figurines on their wishlist because it revolves around a specific franchise they’re a fan of, be it a TV show, movie, book series or sports team. That means there’s a Funko POP! out there for almost everyone. For example, if your giftee loves all things Star Wars, buy them a Funko POP! of their favorite character. I got my brother this one of The Mandalorian a few years ago, which he displays on his bookshelf at home. Anyone who owns a record player will be grateful to unwrap a vinyl from one of their favorite bands or artists. Before I start shopping, I ask my friend or family member to give me a list of options they’re hoping to add to their library — that helps me avoid buying them something they already have. I always look for extra special versions of the vinyls they want, like this glittery orange version of Taylor Swift’s latest album, “The Life of a Showgirl.” There are also exclusive photos and album lyrics on the inside of the jacket. I’m a sucker for a tchotchke, so I naturally fell in love with Dcuk’s wooden statues the minute I saw them. I have five (and counting), and they’re the most asked about pieces of decor in my home — if a loved one notices them, I gift them their first one to start their collection. Each Dcuk stands in a different position, wears a unique outfit and has its own name on the tag. I display them together on a dedicated shelf, but your giftee can also scatter them around their living space and challenge guests to find them as they collect more. Mackenzie-Childs’s black and white Courtly Check line is status symbol kitchen and homeware as far as I’m concerned. It includes pots and pans, countertop appliances, mugs, picture frames and holiday goods like ornaments and stockings — there’s something for you to gift your loved one well into the future if they’re as obsessed with the pattern as other Mackenzie-Child loyalists. The brand’s tea kettle is a solid piece to start their collection because it’s useful for boiling water, and it can stay on their stovetop, acting as a piece of decor. Adding a new ornament to my loved ones’ Christmas trees each year is one of my favorite traditions. In 2025, I personalized an ornament for each family through Artifact Uprising. The brand’s two-sided Pressed Glass Photo Ornament comes in oval, landscape and circle shapes, and you can upload any photo to be printed inside it — I chose to focus on pets in the past, but in 2026, I’m going with snapshots from our most memorable trips. You can also add a tag with the year to mark the keepsake. It comes with a ribbon that helps you hang it on branches. Even though they probably have tons of them, getting a new mug will make the tea- or coffee-drinker in your life excited about sipping their favorite warm beverage. Anthropologie sells dozens of beautifully decorated options, like this one covered in a cityscape illustration.
